raw_response:
I've been farming this land in Quzhou for 25 years, so I know what works. Let me think through this season.

My biggest fields — about 30 mu — I keep in wheat-maize rotation. That's what most people around here do, and I've never had reason to change it. Wheat goes in after the National Day holiday, maize goes in right after wheat harvest in June. Same fields, two crops.

The other 35 mu I split between my cash crops: watermelon (8 mu), chili (10 mu), cabbage (8 mu), and stevia (9 mu). The stevia I have a contract with a company in town — fixed price, they collect it. That's stable income. Chili and watermelon I sell at the county market.

For wheat, I know dealers push the compound fertilizer hard, and I do use it — usually a 50 kg bag of 17-17-17 compound plus some extra urea per mu. My neighbor Old Zhang applies the same and his wheat is always good, around 450 kg per mu. I do 4 irrigations — before sowing to wet the soil, jointing, heading, and grain-filling. Can't skip any of them or yield drops.

For maize I don't plow — I seed it directly into the stubble after wheat, saves time and the soil is already in decent shape. I apply compound fertilizer at sowing and then chase with urea at the big-bell stage. 3 irrigations is usually enough unless it's a dry year.

Watermelon and chili are thirsty crops and they get more diseases. I spray more on them — probably 5 times each season. Watermelon in particular needs potassium for sweetness, so I put extra in there.

Cabbage is autumn crop on those 8 mu — I plant it in August, and it likes nitrogen. I apply a bit more N there than on the grains.

Stevia is the lightest feeder of all my crops. The company told me not to over-fertilize it or the leaves turn too dark and the extraction is worse. So I keep that one moderate — well, actually about 11 kg N per mu, which is lighter than everything else.

I'm spending real money on inputs across 65 mu, so I try not to waste. But I'd rather apply a little extra fertilizer than fall short at harvest. A poor yield means I can't pay the electricity bill for the irrigation well or buy seed next year.
